concept: The answer that cost a Kodiak hunter $150 sat on top of a stack of summaries. Each layer of the stack plays in its own real world, and one continuous dive through the labelled sheets lands on the thick, still regulations and emergency orders underneath.
title: The Answer Was on Top

treatment.winner: dramatist 'The Top of the Stack' revised after Gate 0B
treatment.judge_reasoning: All four lenses converged on a stack of summaries. The dramatist's descent gives the argument a body. Grafts: the enthusiast's admiration beats (she called troopers, the trooper ran the search himself, ADF&G prints its number) and the comedian's physical binder as the bottom text. Gate 0B rejected a back half spent entirely on one paper world, so the stack now appears in one shot only, the dive; the warnings play on a phone, the source-of-truth line in the Public Safety office, and the catch on a laptop at the kitchen table. Comedy is confined to objects, never Weaver or Google's people.

angle.thesis: The answer that cost a Kodiak hunter $150 sat on top of a stack of summaries, and the one binding text, the state's regulation, is what she opened to find the right date and turn herself in.
supporting_facts: c4/c5/c8: opening the regs is how she found Oct 8 and self-reported
c6: the trooper ran the identical search and got the identical wrong answer, so the error repeats for every searcher
c13+c15: even ADF&G calls its online regs simplified, and Google's own page says check more than one place
angle.counterpoint_to_honor: Google's warning and the state's rule both existed and she still paid $150; but a wrong answer that replicates for every searcher (c6) and that DPS expects to see again (c9,c11) is not one hunter's slip. Nothing in the file says what the AI cited, so no claim about Google's sourcing.
angle.falsifiability: False if the trooper's identical search had returned a correct date, or if ADF&G's own published listing said Sept 1 (the booklet did not load, so this is disclosed as unverified).
angle.second_movement: c13 recontextualizes the 'one source of truth' line: it is itself a simplified convenience over the statute, so the honest lesson is a stack of summaries over one binding text, not AI bad and the official page good.
angle.valence: mixed, respectful of Weaver, constructive, no scold, no pile-on at Google
runner_ups: Honesty as the working safeguard (self-report + replication)
Provenance ask: AI answers that name the ADF&G source (booklet did not load so the falsifier is open)
angle.why_runner_ups_lost: each is a sub-beat of the chosen thesis; the provenance ask overreaches the evidence (nothing says what the AI cited)

open_loop.what: a thick peat binder is opened at the kitchen table with its page turned away. The film refuses to show that page until the viewer's hands open the binder and its title strip reads REGULATIONS AND EMERGENCY ORDERS.

open_loop_2.what: So which page can a hunter trust? The question is asked after the answer repeats for the trooper and is withheld until the dive lands on the binder that holds regulations and emergency orders.

divergence_note: Against 2026-09-23 (frontal document, split-compare, divide-and-settle, document-as-subject, dusk violet and copper) and 2026-09-19 (macro-closeup, single-object-void, radial-emanate, structure-as-subject, powerhouse green and amber) this film changes worlds every shot: marsh, kitchen, trooper desk, truck cab, court counter, fogged window, Public Safety wall, phone results, laptop, one stack dive, hands. Paper appears as one continuous vertical CROSS-SECTION DIVE in STACKED-LAYERS, a triple none of the last four films used. Its register is tactile collage, its camera strategy dolly-through, its light overcast-diffuse. Its palette shares no colour role with either and none with the last ten films: slate fog, hunter orange, wet peat umber, cool grey-white paper.
